regime: Trend-Down (Indices Flip Below Their Stops, Havens and Oil Reclaim)
summary: Tech led the tape lower and both index futures lost their trend lines, while the bid rotated into gold and oil. NQ gapped down from Wednesday's close, broke the opening range down just before 10 a.m. Eastern, and closed 31,021.5, off 1.22 percent and below its ATR stop for the first time this week. ES followed it under its own stop, closing 7,822.75 down 0.35 percent, a thinner loss but the same direction. December gold reclaimed its stop and closed 4,158.4 up 0.52 percent, and crude ripped 2.51 percent to 91.17, back above the line it flipped down on yesterday. VIX edged up to near 15.4, still a calm sub-16 read, so this was a rotation day more than a fear day.

risk.sizing: Standard, lean smaller on the range expansion
risk.openRisk: Index trend-long is off, both index futures closed below their stops.
risk.note: Throttle stays NORMAL with VIX sub-16, but the regime flipped today. Both index futures lost their ATR stops, so systematic trend-long on the indices is flat until price reclaims those lines. Gold and crude flipped the other way and are now the trending side. Intraday ranges expanded hard (MNQ one-sigma near 133 points versus 47 on Wednesday), so keep size at the smaller end of standard and let the stop lines decide exposure. The shutdown keeps federal data on hold, so expect headline-driven moves, like today's crude rip, rather than scheduled catalysts.

psychology: Yesterday NQ reversed up off its lows and closed green, and it was tempting to carry that bullish read into today. The market did not care about yesterday. NQ opened lower, lost its stop, and never looked back. When price closes below the line that defined your trend, your bias has to change with it, even when yesterday felt bullish. Write down the level that flips you before the session starts, then let that level, not your memory of yesterday, run the trade.
